review: Independent read-only review of the P19 BF16 ring-phase correction and probe evidence
scope: Host source/artifact review only; no production edits, TTNN imports, device commands, or inference. Resume rerun is still active; its results are intentionally pending.

patch_review.production_change: In MultichipDecoder._reduce_output, prefill ring phase padding is now selected for all prefill dtypes rather than only BFP8; decode and non-Ring paths still select phase zero. In prepare_prefill_ccl, ring warmup is now allowed for BF16, and dummy input dtype is bfloat8_b for BFP8 policy or residual_dtype for the BF16 policy.
patch_review.dtype_correctness: P19 runtime policy has ccl_dtype.prefill=bfloat16 and residual_dtype=bfloat16; existing BFP8 policies have prefill_ccl_bfp8=true. The warmup dummy therefore matches both supported prefill CCL dtypes. _prefill_ccl_zero_rows cache key includes dtype, preventing BF16/BFP8 buffer aliasing.
patch_review.trace_allocation: Generator.prepare_decode calls each layer.prepare_prefill_ccl before beginning model/sample trace captures. It shares padding dictionaries by (hidden, prefill_ccl_bfp8, topology), which separates BF16 from BFP8 and reuses same-policy zero buffers. The new BF16 warmup allocations occur before trace capture. Prefill itself is eager, not replayed as a trace; decode has phase zero. The active resume command enables TT_METAL_TRACE_ALLOC_TRACKING=1 to check runtime trace-allocation behavior.

host_tests.result: 5 tests passed, 0.015s. Tests AST-execute production methods with doubles and cover BF16/BFP8 padding, unchanged decode/non-Ring paths, phase trim shape, warmup dtype, phase restoration, and dtype-keyed zero-row reuse.

probe_evidence.result: 40 comparisons across captured layer-0 BF16 self_attn.o_proj and mlp.down_proj inputs. Exact source slice identity and leading-phase padding parity held for all comparisons; nonzero-phase direct reduction mismatched in 6 comparisons, while phase-256 controls were exact. This supports the local BF16 ring phase mechanism; it does not establish full-model sufficiency.
probe_evidence.limitations: The diagnostic allocated temporary reductions after prepare_decode had captured decode traces but did not replay those traces afterward. It released traces at teardown. This does not prove trace allocation safety; the active full resume rerun with allocation tracking is the relevant check.

patch_review.review_conclusion: The patch is narrowly scoped and consistent with the isolated mechanism. BFP8 behavior is preserved and decode/non-Ring behavior remains unchanged by the new guard. BF16 warmup uses the policy-compatible dtype and is ordered before trace capture. The full-model rerun with tracking completed but still fails the unchanged resume gate at 9/14 cases; phase alignment improves the earliest rows but does not prove sufficiency. Preserve P19 as unselected pending further diagnosis and a passing gate.

resume_rerun.position_observation: At start32, positions32-63 have segment PCC mean .999193, PCC min .997802, top1 31/32; first top1 mismatch is absolute position41. The 64-95 band drops to mean PCC .949524 and top1 26/32; 96-127 drops further to .865404 and 22/32. At start64, the first 64-95 band is .950571/27 of32 and 96-127 is .862533/24 of32. Thus phase correction improves the earliest prefix-aligned rows but later chunk rows still diverge.
resume_rerun.trace_tracking: The run was admitted with TT_METAL_TRACE_ALLOC_TRACKING=1. It reached the normal statistical-gate failure and exited after closing devices; the captured log contains no trace-allocation exception or process/runtime error. This is evidence that this execution completed under tracking, not a general proof that all trace paths are allocation-safe.
resume_rerun.interpretation: The BF16 ring phase probe supports the local mechanism, and the full-model rerun shows improved early rows, but the unchanged resume acceptance remains failed (9/14 failures). This patch is insufficient to establish resumed-prefill equivalence. Continue stage capture; do not select P19 or relax thresholds.
